gap: No result ChatGPT got prices the in-dash CD receivers (Pioneer DEH-S4220BT, Sony MEX-N5300BT, Kenwood KDC-BT282U) from the maker's US store today. I could not open those prices either, so this angle has no new priced fact to add.
standout_why: I compared against itechguides.com (2026-10-11) and ensightauto.com (2026-02-04). Itechguides already prices five portable or external players ($34.99 to $65.89) and states the reason each loses: no Bluetooth into the car, no USB audio out, or AUX only. Ensightauto already says to budget $200 to $400 for a USB CD kit and that most 2016-and-newer touchscreen cars qualify. Neither page prices an in-dash single-DIN CD receiver or FiiO's DM13. My pricing would have filled that gap, but every maker and retailer page I tried blocked me, so what I can source only partly repeats the rivals.
decides: It confirms the split in our current page and in ChatGPT's answer. A cheap portable player only reaches the car through AUX or FM: itechguides quotes the Sunoony listing's 'No USB audio output to vehicle' and MEGATEK's 'Not compatible with Bluetooth car stereos'. A USB external drive needs a head unit that reads USB CD drives, and ensightauto says to spend $200 to $400. An in-dash receiver is the sure path for a single-DIN car. I could not open today's price for any candidate, so the price ranking between the paths is not settled.
